doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Music as a crutch that takes away life's pain
summary: Rowe quotes Gibbs' book on music as a crutch; Gibbs says playing takes your mind off troubles.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well I’m going to turn to the book of Gibbs here, because it reminded me of something that I circled. And you wrote, “ For most musicians playing music is a crutch. If you have nothing else happening in your life at least you know you can play music. Things are bad for whatever reason, your wife left you, you’re not making any money, you can’t pay the mortgage, you can always pick up your horn and play. It gives you something that you can’t buy.”

Because it takes your mind off of everything. It just — you cannot play the jazz if you’re not into the music. While I’m playing if I don’t hear the next note — you know when you read a newspaper how you read ahead sometimes? It’s almost like reading. That’s what happens, like with music. You almost hear ahead. And so if I’m thinking about my divorce or alimony or whatever, I can’t play. And you’re not thinking. That takes away all the pain of everything going on in your life when you play. The moment you finish playing your chorus you may start crying, but while you’re playing your chorus you’re as happy as a lark you know.
